correctness.rationale: For the signed Schur multiplier M_(n,k) with negative first k diagonal entries, an explicit nonnegative vector u gives trace-norm lower bound ||diag(u) M diag(u)||_1, and positive semidefinite P±M with diagonal T gives factorization upper bound T. The fully flipped k-core has eigenvalues (k−2)/k once and −2/k repeated k−1. With one additional unflipped coordinate, explicit maximizer a_k and 2x2 Gram block determinants yield T=1+k/(1+sqrt(2k)) for 1<=k<=5, versus 3−4/k for k>=6. Replication of the unflipped Gram vectors proves no dependence on further n. Checked n=k=1 and k=0 separately; independently recomputed eigenvalue/witness and PSD certificates for k=1..30, including transition at six. Infinite proof is symbolic positive semidefiniteness, not those finite checks.
